resources.string: Bubble for dictating and inserting text in any app

Amber uses this service to show the dictation bubble and to type your dictation into the field you are writing in. For that it reads which app is in front and whether a text field has focus (to show or hide the bubble), where the keyboard is (to keep the bubble above it), and - only when inserting a dictation - the text already in that field, so the new words fit in at the cursor. None of this is stored or sent anywhere: only your recording, and with cleanup its text, goes to the engine you chose. Right after you switch on something Amber sent you to Android\'s settings for - this service, or battery use without limits - it brings Amber back to the front. Beyond that it never taps, swipes or acts for you - unless you switch on voice commands in Amber. Then it carries out only the command you just spoke: go back or home, show recent apps or quick settings, show or close notifications, lock the screen, take a screenshot, split the screen, show the power menu, open an app or a settings page (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, display, battery - it only opens them, never switches anything there), scroll, page or swipe, press play, pause or skip, change or mute the volume, switch the flashlight, and edit the field you started the command in (delete words, select all, copy, cut, paste, start a new line). For that it reads your list of apps and which app came to the front after it opened one, which parts of the screen can scroll and - in the one it scrolls - where the items sit, to tell whether it moved (never what they show), the volume and whether the flashlight is on, and, only for a command that edits text, the text of that field, never in a password field; all on the phone only. It never taps buttons or confirms dialogs; a swipe does what your own swipe would do in that app - in a mail list it may archive a mail.
